brief.subject: CFPB targets large-bank debanking; secured card approval data
brief.headline: CFPB Opens New Push on Debanking by Large Banks
brief.dek: The CFPB is acting on debanking cases uncovered by the OCC, and new application data shows secured card approvals by credit score band.
brief.lede: The CFPB has announced a new initiative on debanking at large banks, building on findings from the OCC, the national bank regulator.

sections.heading: CFPB Takes Aim at Debanking
bullets: The CFPB announced a new initiative on October 14 targeting debanking by large banks.
The effort builds on debanking cases the OCC uncovered, so it focuses on the biggest institutions.
Debanking means closing or refusing accounts; the CFPB's focus is on decisions tied to constitutionally protected rights.
The bureau calls this the next step in its work against debanking of businesses and individuals, signaling more action may follow.

sections.heading: Secured Card Approvals by Credit Score
bullets: New application data breaks down secured credit card approval rates by credit score band.
Secured cards require a deposit and are a common tool for building or rebuilding credit.
Results come from real applications, giving a practical view of how scores affect approval odds.

brief.seo_description: CFPB launches a new initiative on large-bank debanking uncovered by the OCC, plus data on secured credit card approvals by credit score band.
